payload.claim: The `written` set at line 589-594 queries every `end_reviews` row for a layer's `task_key`, not just its two end-review lenses (`spec`, `standards`). The top layer's task_key is also where `review_joins` files the `join` lens (`saffron/end_review.py:480-492`), and the join lens runs and is recorded before any layer review starts (`run_end_review`'s docstring, `saffron/end_review.py:521-529`). So if a raise reaches this fallback after the join succeeded but before either of the top layer's own lenses was written (e.g. `record_findings` or the first `record_end_review` in `review_stack`'s loop fails), `written` is non-empty because of the unrelated `join` row, and line 595 wrongly appends the note "this layer's rows were written first" to both the `spec` and `standards` errors even though neither was actually written. This mislabels the ledger's diagnostic text for a fairly reachable interleaving that none of this spec's tests drive (all five witness cases either raise before any write, or write only a lens inside `end_review.END_LENSES`, never `join`).
